image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Rock Beauty fish (Holocanthus tricolor). The image captures the anterior to mid-section of the fish, showing the characteristic black head and front body transitioning into a bright yellow posterior. The eye is visible on the far left edge, and the dorsal fin runs along the top with a blueish iridescent margin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small protrusible mouth with brush-like teeth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is located at the very tip of the snout, which is cut off by the left edge of the frame. It is impossible to verify the presence of brush-like teeth or the specific shape of the mouth.
The eye is partially visible on the extreme left edge. While cropped, the visible portion shows a large, dark pupil and iris consistent with the 'large eyes' description of the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed disc-shaped body with compact proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible curvature of the dorsal and ventral profiles indicates a deep, laterally compressed body typical of angelfish/butterflyfish. The proportions appear correct for the class.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Striking gold and black coloration: anterior body and head black, posterior body and tail golden yellow with black margin.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the diagnostic color pattern: a solid black mask covering the head and anterior body, sharply contrasting with the bright yellow/gold of the posterior body. A faint dark margin is visible on the dorsal fin edge.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Continuous dorsal fin with spiny anterior and soft-rayed posterior portions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is visible running along the top. It appears continuous. While individual spines vs. rays are hard to distinguish at this resolution, the structural continuity is present.
The anal fin is located on the ventral side, which is largely obscured by shadow and the angle of the crop. It cannot be clearly evaluated.
The caudal peduncle and tail are completely outside the frame on the right side.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The black scales exhibit a slightly uniform, noisy texture that lacks the distinct individual scale definition seen in high-quality macro photography, suggesting mild AI smoothing or texture synthesis artifacts.

The background is heavily blurred (bokeh), which is natural, but the transition between the fish's lower yellow body and the background shows slight edge bleeding/haloing, indicative of generative blending rather than optical depth of field.
